turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: I just wanted to start with what brings you here today to the family clinic?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Hi, this morning I read after I woke up by I coughed up some phlegm and there was some blood in it and it it totally scared me.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and was this the first time that happened?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, yeah, I've never I never noticed blood in my sputum before.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, but have you been coughing recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh yeah, I have, uh, had a cough recently leading up to this.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and how long have you had the cough for?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I've had it for uhm, yeah, about about four weeks.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Wow, four weeks. OK. Do you know if you did anything prior to that, any new exposures or being around someone ill like anything like that that might have caused your cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I was just down in a, I went to Haiti on a on a trip for a, for a volunteer program with my school and I don't know I definitely notice there is a lot of people down there coughing.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and were you at all living like close quarters or were you crammed into like like smaller spaces at all when you were there?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, we were kind of like living with the locals while we while we were there. It was part of the experience for volunteering. I was there for almost two months as part of, part of my my summer break through University.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and did you notice, uh, at all any potential exposures to tuberculosis? Anyone there that had tuberculosis? Or found out later?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, there were definitely some people around that I heard of who who mentioned tuberculosis, but I don't know if anybody specifically who had it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And the cough that you've been having for the last four weeks at, is it like a wet cough? Are you producing any sputum or phlegm, or is it more of a dry cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, I have been producing some phlegm, um, but it's been just kind of white, yellowish.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Up until this morning?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah or moreso clear actually, up until today where I saw some blood.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And how much blood was in the phlegm? Was it like a significant amount it filled the whole production or just little streaks?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um it was pretty red. It, ah, yeah it was bright red and it was covering the, the issue.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK and have you had any similar episodes before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I've never brought up blood before.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: And after this morning, was that the only time you had that or did you did it recur at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, it was just that time just this morning on the tissue and then a little bit in the toilet and it looked like a lot in the in the water.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, I see and how often are you coughing in like an average day? Are you coughing throughout the day or does it come and go?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, it's been pretty severe through throughout the day. I've been just coughing or coughing a ton.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, anything that makes your coughing go away or makes it worse at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not-nothing seems to help. I've tried various over the counter medications and and stuff for, for cough and nothing has seemed to help it.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and are you having any other symptoms at all, like shortness of breath, sore throat, runny nose, anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, nothing like like that. I mean the back of my throat, might feel a little itchy from the coughing, but not really sure.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Are you having any headaches or nausea or vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Nothing like, well, a little bit of nausea maybe, but no vomiting.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. How often you getting nausea?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, it's coming after like if I'm having a really big cough, coughing fit I could feel a little nauseous after but it doesn't last very long.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, are you having any fevers or chills?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I've been having ah, so fevers throughout the day, but feeling really hot, and and really sweaty at night.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how often are you getting night sweats?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, also a few times this past week, I've what woke up soaked.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And have you at all measured when you felt, measured your temperature when you felt like these chills and night sweats?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I haven't measured my temperature yet.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Have you noticed at all, uh, any increased fatigue throughout the day?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, but I've definitely been more more tired. I haven't been able to concentrate on, umm, on my schoolwork.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And, um, have you been having any shortness of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Just after the, like coughing really, but otherwise, ah, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any chest pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No chest pain.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any feeling that your heart is racing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any swelling in your limbs at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Ok. Any loss of sense of taste or smell?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any changes in your bowel movements?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any changes in your urination?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any changes at all in your sleep?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, just been, well, I haven't been sleeping as well, waking up all sweaty and the cough is kept me up a little bit too.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any changes in your appetite?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, I've been eating OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Have you noticed at all any weight loss over the last few months?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I think I'm down like 15 pounds since the summer time, which is great.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, have you tried to lose weight at all or is it just been completely unintentional?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, well I, I mean my, my appendix was taken out a few months ago and so I guess after that I, well, maybe wasn't eating and eating as much, but I mean I wasn't really trying to lose weight.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and have you had any recent exposure to any fumes or dust or animals?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, my my parents have a dog at home, but I've been away at school, so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. OK, uh, in terms of your overall health, have you been diagnosed with any medical conditions before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, I'm uh, healthy.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: So like no asthma or anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, nothing like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, are you on any medications currently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh. Yeah, I take an oral contraceptive pill.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK um, and when did you start that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Probably about five years ago.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Do you have any allergies, to any medications or any environmental allergies at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, yeah, I think Septra, gives me a rash.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Um, any previous hospitalizations?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I've never been in the hospital before.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any previous surgery? So you said you had the appendix removed but anything else?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no the appendix was the only thing.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Any family history of asthma or any lung conditions? Any cancers that run in the family?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Um, yeah but well, my grandfather had lung cancer, but he smoked for his entire life. And my mom has had diabetes for quite some time, but no, no lung problems.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any heart attacks in the family or any autoimmune conditions?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and currently what is your living situation like?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: So I live with uh, four roommates here going to school.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and so do you work right now or you just a student right now?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Just a student.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And currently do you smoke?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I'mm smoke maybe maybe socially so, maybe a pack of cigarettes a week at the at the most.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. And any recreational drug use like marijuana?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, yeah I'll smoke one or two joints on on the weekend with friends socially.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK yeah, so yeah. This uh, the smoking marijuana or cigarettes make your symptoms worse at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, it depends. Yeah, sometimes I can. It can bring on some more coughing.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, so yeah, we always recommend cutting down or quitting smoking whenever, whenever we see patients who are smoking, especially like, you're fairly young. And you know your grandfather had history of lung cancer with smoking throughout the year. So as early as we can quit smoking, the better for the long term health of your lungs, but whenever you're thinking of quitting, or if you want any more resources about quitting, just let me know. We can set up a separate appointment for that.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK, that that sounds good. Yeah, maybe maybe next appointment we can talk about that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, sounds good. Um. Any, uh, so no recreational, so just besides marijuana. Any other recreational drugs like cocaine or crystal meth, anything of that sort?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Ah, no. Well, sometimes I at parties maybe a few times a year with friends will use ecstasy or something like that, but that's only a few times a year.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Uh, and any alcohol?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I'll have a few drinks on the weekend with with friends usually. Like rum or beer.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Yeah, so this is all the questions I had for you today. Any, any questions or concerns or any ideas of what you think this might be?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, I don't know. I'm really concerned about the the blood that I brought up like I mean is this cancer or, uh, uh tuberculosis like one of those tuberculosis infections that I heard about while I was away?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, so definitely, a cancer is pretty unlikely because you're fairly young and you've just recently started smoking, but one of the things that we're concerned about is your recent travel history being in close quarters. So definitely we need to get a chest X-Ray and we can even do a sputum culture to test for tuberculosis. And then based on the results, we might have to start you on like a whole antibiotic regiment if it does come back as tuberculosis. Yeah, we'll, we'll, we'll get those investigations done first and then we'll go from there.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK, thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: We'll also get some blood work done as well, so that'll be done before your next appointment.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Alright, that sounds good. Thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: You're welcome.
